prompt: Why does the lesson run the five databases one at a time?

choices.text: Docker runs one container at a time
choices.why: The box office runs four at once.

choices.text: Together they want more memory than the lab should give
choices.why: Right. One at a time, the largest takes about a gigabyte.

choices.text: They use the same port
choices.why: None of them publishes a port in this lesson.

choices.text: Each one would overwrite the data the previous one left in the shared volume
choices.why: Each lives in its own container.

prompt: What is DynamoDB Local, as used here?

choices.text: An open-source fork of DynamoDB
choices.why: Amazon publishes it for testing; it is not the service's code.

choices.text: A program that answers DynamoDB's interface on your machine
choices.why: Right, without the service's partitions, throttling or bill.

choices.text: A copy of the AWS service, with its partitions and limits reproduced on a smaller scale
choices.why: It reproduces the interface, not the distribution or the limits.

choices.text: A cache in front of the real service that keeps a copy of recent items
choices.why: It talks to nothing in the cloud.

choices.text: A second filter, applied after the first one has run

prompt: What does the path "venue.name" let a MongoDB query do?

choices.text: Filter on a field of an embedded document

choices.text: Read the venue from another database

choices.text: Rename the field

prompt: A document is inserted with venu instead of venue. What happens?

choices.text: It is stored, and never matches a query on venue.name
choices.why: Right, unless the collection enforces a JSON Schema.

choices.text: MongoDB refuses it
choices.why: Nothing declared the shape, so nothing refuses it.

choices.text: The whole collection is rewritten with the new field name added to every document
choices.why: Documents are independent; nothing else changes.

choices.text: MongoDB corrects the field name to the closest one it already knows
choices.why: It does not guess.

prompt: Before the index, the query for Teatro Ipê examined 100 documents and returned 34. Which stage was that?

choices.text: COLLSCAN
choices.why: Right: every document read.

choices.text: FETCH

choices.text: IXSCAN
choices.why: That came after createIndex, examining 34.

choices.text: SORT
choices.why: There was no sort in that query.

prompt: updateMany renamed the venue in 33 documents. What can a reader in the middle see?

choices.text: Some shows with the old name and some with the new
choices.why: Right. Each document changes atomically; the 33 are not one transaction.

choices.text: A document with half the venue changed
choices.why: Single-document writes are atomic.

choices.text: An error, because the collection is locked while the update runs over its documents
choices.why: Reads continue during updateMany.

choices.text: Only the old name, until all 33 are done
choices.why: That would need a transaction across documents.

prompt: How many documents did the indexed query examine?
Why is the sort key written as show-1#seat-42 rather than seat-42#show-1?

choices.text: The # character must come in the middle of a key
choices.why: # is a convention, not a requirement.

choices.text: It makes each item cheaper to write, because the shorter part is compressed first
choices.why: The order changes how it is read, not what it costs to write.

choices.text: DynamoDB requires the longest part first
choices.why: No such rule exists.

choices.text: So one buyer's tickets for a show sit together in sort order
choices.why: Right. begins_with narrows by the leading part.

prompt: Why does DynamoDB send numbers, like cents, as strings in its requests?

choices.text: So that no precision is lost on the way
choices.why: Right. A JSON number can be read as a float by the client.

choices.text: Because YAML has no numbers
choices.why: The rule is DynamoDB's, in JSON too.

choices.text: Because the attribute was declared as S
choices.why: cents is N; only the transport is a string.

choices.text: So that they sort as text
choices.why: N attributes sort as numbers.

prompt: A query names only the sort key. What does DynamoDB answer?

choices.text: Every item that matches the condition, just more slowly
choices.why: There is no fallback to reading everything.

choices.text: A ValidationException: the partition key is missing
choices.why: Right. A query must name the partition.

choices.text: An empty result
choices.why: It refuses rather than answering empty.

choices.text: The first item of each partition, in the order the partitions are stored on disk
choices.why: Nothing like that exists.

prompt: A scan with a filter returned 3 items with ScannedCount 5. What is the capacity charged on?

choices.text: The 5 items read
choices.why: Right. The filter runs after the read.

choices.text: The 3 items returned
choices.why: Returned items are a subset of what was paid for.

choices.text: Nothing, scans are free
choices.why: They are the most expensive reads.

choices.text: The size of the filter expression, counted in characters and billed per thousand
choices.why: Capacity is about data read.

prompt: A global secondary index keyed by ticket is added. Right after a sale, a query on the index does not show it. Why?

choices.text: The sale was written to the wrong partition and has to be moved before the index sees it
choices.why: The sale is where its key put it; the index is simply behind.

choices.text: The index is updated asynchronously
choices.why: Right: lesson 2's replica lag in a new place.

choices.text: Indexes only contain items older than a day
choices.why: They follow the table, a moment behind.

choices.text: Queries on an index need a scan first
choices.why: They are queries like any other.

choices.text: Only three scans existed
choices.why: Show 1 had five.

choices.text: Cassandra keeps an index on scanned_at

choices.text: cqlsh sorts the result by time before printing it, as a convenience for the reader
choices.why: The shell prints what the node returns.

choices.why: Nothing is rounded.

choices.text: cqlsh prints UTC, three hours ahead of São Paulo
choices.why: Right. Same instant, another clock.

prompt: In a cluster with three replicas, a write at ONE and a read at ONE. What can the read miss?

choices.text: Nothing; ONE always reads the newest
choices.why: ONE reads whichever replica answers first.
